how.text: Keeps every memory on this computer, in its own process, and finds related ones with a vector index.
Memories are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a random key the OS keystore protects.
If the computer has no keystore, memory stays unencrypted and the app says so, rather than writing the key in plain text.

why.text: Loading a large memory store took seconds; in its own process that cost never touches typing.
Secrets are scrubbed in the main process before a memory is sent here, so they never enter this process.

glossary.React: The library that builds the app's screens out of small components.
glossary.xterm.js: The terminal emulator that draws text, colours and the cursor in each pane.
glossary.Monaco: The code editor from VS Code, used to edit shell config files.
glossary.three.js: A 3D drawing library for the web; it draws this city.
glossary.WebGL: The browser's way to draw 3D with the graphics card.
glossary.MessagePort: A private two-way pipe between two parts of the app.
glossary.Electron: Runs a web-technology app as a desktop program, with a main process and windows.
glossary.IPC: Messages between the app's window and its main process.
glossary.node-pty: Gives a program a real terminal, so shells and agents behave as they would in any terminal.
glossary.utilityProcess: A separate helper process Electron starts; if it is busy or crashes, the window keeps working.
glossary.worker thread: A second thread inside a process, for heavy work that must not block the first.
glossary.tree-sitter: A fast parser that reads source code into a tree of functions and calls.
glossary.JSONL: A log file with one JSON record per line; agents write their sessions this way.
glossary.headless agent: An AI agent run in the background with no window, for one job.
glossary.HNSW: An index that finds the nearest vectors quickly, so similar memories are found fast.
glossary.AES-256-GCM: A standard cipher that both hides data and detects any change to it.
glossary.OS keystore: Where the operating system keeps secrets: DPAPI on Windows, Keychain on macOS, libsecret on Linux.
glossary.ONNX Runtime: Runs a machine-learning model on your own computer, here as WebAssembly.
glossary.bge-small: A small open embedding model (bge-small-en-v1.5) that turns text into 384 numbers.
glossary.cross-encoder: A model that reads a question and a result together and scores how well they match.
glossary.TLS: The encryption that protects a connection (the S in HTTPS and WSS).
glossary.MCP: Model Context Protocol: the standard way an AI agent calls tools.
glossary.stdio: A program's standard input and output, used here as a private pipe to the agent.
glossary.X25519: A key agreement method: two devices make a shared secret without sending it.
glossary.ChaCha20-Poly1305: An authenticated cipher that seals each message so only the other device can read it.
glossary.WebSocket: A long-lived two-way connection over the web.
glossary.gh CLI: GitHub's own command-line tool, signed in with your account.

steps.caption: The Screen: terminals, settings, the workflow designer and this view, all in one window.
The Core: the main process stays light, and starts helpers for terminals and other programs.
Memory: what your agents learn, kept and searched on this computer, encrypted where a keystore exists.
The token proxy: a local program that shrinks what Claude Code sends.
The agent gateway: the tools Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI can call.
Remote and linked machines: off until you turn them on, sealed end to end.
Lumopolis itself: it reads the code and draws this map.
You type in a pane. On Windows the key takes a private line to the terminal host, past the main process.
The terminal host hands it to the agent running in that terminal.
Claude Code sends its request to the local token proxy.
The proxy shrinks big tool results and forwards the request to Anthropic. The reply streams back untouched.
Your agents talk to their own model providers, under their own sign-in.
Update checks go to GitHub Releases, at launch and every 4 hours.
Crash reports only if you agree to them.
The relay only when Remote is on, and it cannot read what it forwards.
